ing: with 0.5 cup of their cooking liquid
st: Dice the onion and bell pepper into small even pieces and mince the garlic.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large wide skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until soft.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the beans and [[0.5 cup]] of their liquid, then mash a few beans against the pan with your spoon.
Simmer for 5 minutes so the liquid reduces and the beans turn thick and saucy.
Add the cold rice in two batches, breaking up clumps, and drizzle in the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil.
Stir and fold for 5 to 7 minutes until the rice is evenly colored and heated through.
Season with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and pepper, taste, and serve hot with eggs, cheese or fried plantains.

ing: sour orange if you can find it
or 1 tsp paprika plus 1 tsp cumin
about 12 inch squares, softened over a flame, or use foil and parchment
st: Mix the pork with the orange juice, achiote paste, garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt. Marinate for at least 1 hour or overnight in the fridge.
In a bowl, mix the masa harina with [[0.5 tsp]] salt and the lard. Slowly add the warm broth, kneading until you have a soft, spreadable dough like thick mashed potatoes.
Soften the banana leaves by passing them briefly over a gas flame or dipping in hot water. Wipe them dry and lay one flat.
Spread about [[0.5 cup]] of masa in a thin square in the middle of the leaf.
Top with a piece of pork, a spoonful of soaked rice, a few potato slices, a tomato slice, and an onion and pepper ring.
Cover with a little more masa, then fold the leaf over the filling like a parcel and wrap it again in a second leaf.
Tie each bundle firmly with twine in both directions so it stays closed.
Stand the bundles in a large pot, cover with hot water and simmer gently, adding water as needed, for 3 hours.
Lift out the nacatamales with tongs and let them rest 10 minutes. The pork should be tender (145°F/63°C or higher) and the masa firm.
Unwrap and serve hot on the leaf, with bread on the side. Do not eat the banana leaf.

ing: peeled, cut into chunks, woody core removed
st: Put the cassava in a large pot, cover with water and add [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil.
Boil for 25 to 30 minutes until a knife slides in easily. Drain and keep warm.
Mix the vinegar, [[1 cup]] water, [[0.5 tsp]] salt and lime juice in a bowl to make a light brine.
Add the cabbage, tomatoes and chili. Toss and let the slaw sit for at least 20 minutes.
Roast the pork rinds in a warm pan for a few minutes if they have gone soft, then chop them roughly.
Lay banana leaf pieces on plates and pile on warm cassava chunks.
Spoon the drained slaw over the cassava.
Top with the chopped pork rinds just before serving so they stay crunchy.
Put the beef, half the onion and [[6 cups]] water in a large pot with [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil, then lower to a simmer.
Cover and simmer for about 1.5 hours until the beef shreds easily.
Lift out the beef and shred it with two forks. Keep the broth.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the remaining onion, bell pepper and garlic for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes until they break down.
Stir the masa harina into [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth, then pour it in along with [[3 cups]] of the beef broth.
Add the shredded beef and orange juice. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick like a stew.
Stir in the mint, remaining [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper. Add a splash more broth if it gets too thick.
Rest for 5 minutes, then serve with rice or tostones.

ing: rinsed well and cut into small pieces
one halved for rinsing, one for serving
st: Rinse the tripe under cold water, rub it with lime halves, rinse again and cut it into bite-size pieces.
Put the tripe in a large pot with the water, half the onion, half the garlic and [[1 tsp]] salt. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam.
Cover and simmer gently for about 2.5 hours until the tripe is very tender.
Add the bell pepper, tomatoes, carrots, cassava and the remaining onion and garlic.
Simmer for 20 minutes, then add the plantains and corn.
Cook for another 20 minutes until the cassava and plantains are soft.
Season with the remaining [[1 tsp]] salt and the pepper, then stir in the cilantro.
Serve hot in deep bowls with lime wedges and a little rice on the side.

ing: or mozzarella string cheese, in strips
st: Mix the vinegar, [[0.5 cup]] water, [[0.25 tsp]] salt and lime juice in a bowl.
Add the sliced onion and let it pickle for at least 15 minutes.
Stir the sour cream with the milk and [[0.25 tsp]] salt until pourable.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet for 30 seconds per side until soft and flexible.
Lay a quarter of the cheese down the middle of each tortilla.
Top with a handful of drained pickled onions.
Drizzle with the cream and roll up the tortilla tightly.
Serve right away while the tortilla is warm.

ing: peeled and cut in thick rounds
large, softened over a flame, or use foil
st: Rub the beef with the garlic, salt, pepper and orange juice. Marinate for at least 1 hour or overnight in the fridge.
Soften the banana leaves over a flame or in hot water, then lay them criss-cross in a large heavy pot with the edges hanging over.
Place a few plantain slices on the leaves, then lay the beef on top.
Cover the beef with onion rings, tomato and bell pepper slices.
Add the cassava and the rest of the plantains, then pour in [[1 cup]] water.
Fold the leaf edges over the top and cover tightly with more leaves, then foil, then the pot lid.
Cook over low heat for about 4 hours, checking now and then that the pot does not dry out.
Open carefully and check the beef is very tender. Slice or pull it apart and serve with the vegetables and juices.
Cut the ends off each plantain, slice through the peel lengthwise and pry it off. Cut into rounds about 1 inch thick.
Heat the oil in a deep skillet over medium heat to 325°F (160°C).
Fry the rounds for 3 minutes per side until pale golden and tender in the middle. Transfer to paper towels.
Stir the garlic, lime juice, warm water and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together in a small bowl.
Press each fried round flat to about half its thickness with a flat-bottomed glass or plate.
Dip each flattened round briefly in the garlic water and pat dry.
Raise the heat to 375°F (190°C) and fry the flattened rounds for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and sprinkle with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Serve hot.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt in a bowl.
Beat the egg yolks with [[1 cup]] sugar for 3 minutes until pale and thick. Mix in [[0.25 cup]] of the whole milk and [[1 tsp]] vanilla, then fold in the flour.
In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites to soft peaks, then add [[0.25 cup]] sugar a little at a time and whip to stiff peaks.
Gently fold the whites into the batter in three parts, keeping it airy. Pour into the pan.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes until golden and a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Whisk the condensed milk, evaporated milk, [[0.75 cup]] of the remaining whole milk and [[0.5 cup]] cream together.
Poke the cake all over with a fork, then slowly pour the milk mixture over it. Chill for at least 4 hours.
Whip the remaining [[1.5 cups]] cream with [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] vanilla to soft peaks. Spread on top and dust with cinnamon.

ing: if using plain cornmeal, toast it dry first
st: If using plain cornmeal, toast it in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, until it smells nutty and turns light brown. This takes about 5 minutes.
Mix the toasted cornmeal, cocoa, cinnamon and allspice in a bowl.
Whisk in the cold water a little at a time to make a smooth paste with no lumps.
Pour the milk into a saucepan and heat until steaming, but do not boil.
Whisk the paste into the hot milk.
Simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, whisking often, until slightly thickened.
Stir in the sugar until dissolved and taste for sweetness.
Serve warm, or chill and pour over ice. Stir before drinking since the corn settles.
Butterfly each steak lengthwise so it opens up about 1/2 inch thick. Season both sides with [[1 tsp]] salt and pepper and rest 20 minutes.
Make the chimichurri: mix the parsley, garlic, onion, [[0.25 cup]] vinegar, [[0.5 cup]] olive oil, oregano, pepper flakes and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Let it sit 15 minutes.
Heat a grill to very high, about 500°F. Clean and oil the grate lightly.
Grill the steaks 2 to 3 minutes per side for medium rare (135°F) or 4 minutes per side for medium, turning once, until deeply charred.
Rest the steaks 5 minutes on a board, then slice against the grain.
Spoon the chimichurri over the meat and serve with gallo pinto, fried plantains and cabbage salad.
nt: Grilled over very high direct heat, quick sear
Best swap: sear in a ripping hot cast iron pan 2 to 3 minutes per side. Flank or skirt steak replaces tenderloin.
